answer: Each identity stakes a 70-credit bond and, at dawn, gets a key-bound dune puzzle: find a nonce hashing its key, a distinct juniper tag, and the dawn time to the auditor target. The auditor checks all three; a reused tag or late answer burns the bond. The first puzzle costs 34 credits; the kth costs 34+6(k-1), as the auditor tightens the target for each later claim in the same dune dawn window, so 1,000 fakes pay 3,031,000 plus 70,000 locked. A rented compute farm fails: puzzles cannot be shared, and the window closes before a farm solves many. An honest agent pays once, then redeems the bond.
